title: Space Harrier
build: Elite PAL, Jazzcat Cracking Team D64

records.c: Clear the score and audio request state, select stage one and set the packed-decimal timer to 60. Prepare the score cursor sprite and VIC bank, draw the HUD, install the raster interrupts and enter the title.
Wait for title fire, then reset the score, scrolling state, stage, ten lives, BCD timer and timer divider. Clear object and projectile slots before showing the stage card.

Poll movement and fire between synchronized slices of object updates, sprite setup, terrain drawing and projectile rendering. The status panel is redrawn after decrementing the training timer. A negative remaining-life count routes to the score table.
Clear the pending sprite motion and wait through release, another $EF read and a final release from CIA1 port B before returning to the play loop.
Process the final score and go back to the title setup.
Eight retained values between the game loop and the running sprite-pair table.
Two sprite-pointer pairs for the running animation. Bit 2 of the raster tick counter chooses the pair.
Lower sprite indices for the two running frames are the second and fourth bytes of the pair table.
Return to the game loop while the boss flag suppresses the horizon.

Select two rows of stage scenery from the pointers indexed by stage. Use the current horizontal phase as the source column, then copy 40 character codes to each screen row and colour the rows with values 9 and 12. Skip drawing while the flag at $4EBB is nonzero.
Twelve pointers to scrolling upper horizon rows, indexed by the zero-based stage.
High bytes of the upper horizon source pointers, interleaved with their low bytes in the table at $0A37.
Twelve pointers to scrolling lower horizon rows, indexed by the zero-based stage.
High-byte view of the lower source pointer table used by the horizon renderer.
Two words after the twelve stages in the documented lower horizon table. The stage index wraps before these additional entries.
Upper horizon row data for Moot, Revi, Asute. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Lower horizon row data for Moot, Revi, Asute. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Upper horizon row data for Geeza, Minea. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Lower horizon row data for Geeza, Minea. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Upper horizon row data for Ceiciel, Vicel. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Lower horizon row data for Ceiciel, Vicel. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Upper horizon row data for Ida, Absymbel. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Lower horizon row data for Ida, Absymbel. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Two zero bytes preceding the source row at $0D91. A pointer after the twelve indexed lower-horizon entries points at these two cells.
Upper horizon row data for Amar, Drail, Nark. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Lower horizon row data for Amar, Drail, Nark. The renderer takes a 40-cell window from the 100 screen codes.
Copy the 64-byte cursor sprite seed to VIC slot $B1 at $EC40.
Sprite source for the outlined selection cursor used on the high-score entry screen.

Compare the incoming packed-decimal score with the seven drawn ranks. Move lower scores and ties down with their name fields. A score below seventh writes the spare score word and returns. A qualifying name is entered in a scratch buffer before it is copied to the insertion slot.
Convert sprite 0's position to the screen-cell address that holds the selectable glyph, and save that screen code at $4EC9.
Set sprite 0 to ($F0,$80) with shape $B1 and colour $0E, initialize the eight name cells to $D6 and reset the current name position.
Read the direction bits from joystick port 2 and set signed two-pixel cursor velocities within the selector's coordinate bounds.
Clear each cursor velocity independently when its coordinate reaches a multiple of 16.
Stop the music gates, load the title character bank and print the high-score heading from $10C4. Within that layout $FF advances the destination to the next row and $80 ends the stream.
Set up the score cursor and music, then poll selection and movement after each raster tick until the selected cell is the finish glyph $FD.
High-score entry display template, including the alphabet grid. Byte $FF ends a row and $80 ends the template.
Edge-detect joystick fire. Read the glyph under the selector, erase a letter for $FC or append the glyph to the name and screen. Stop at eight name cells.
Apply the pending signed X and Y increments to sprite 0.
Give the screen a uniform colour, then write seven rows containing rank, eight name characters, four score digits and two trailing zeros.
Copy the selected four-character rank field to the destination row. Preserve the rank index in X.
Copy eight stored screen codes from the name indexed by X.
Read two stored BCD bytes and output their four glyph codes into the destination row.
Seven consecutive four-character fields for the ranks 1ST through 7TH.
An eighth field holding 8TH, beyond the seven rows drawn by the score-table loop.
Eight seeded name slots, each eight screen codes. The score renderer shows the first seven and the insertion loop may shift into the eighth.
The second seeded name is MARK followed by four blank cells. This address is also the destination base for shifting names down one entry.
Eight blank glyph codes just before the writable score words.
Clear the playfield screen to zero and fill the colour field with the incoming Y value, leaving the HUD row intact.
Initialize music, select title graphics from $C800, draw the logo and copyright text, and wait for port 2 fire. A timeout branches to the high-score display and then rebuilds the title.
Twenty-four title credit cells spelling ELITE SYSTEMS LTD 1986 with a copyright glyph and leading space.
Twenty-seven title credit cells spelling SEGA ENTERPRISES LTD 1985 with a copyright glyph and leading space.
Nineteen screen codes spelling PRESS FIRE TO START.

Read a width and height from the first two source bytes, then copy one screen code per cell, restarting each destination row 40 bytes below the preceding one. X and Y choose the upper-left screen column and row.

Run a short forced-descent transition, advance the BCD stage number and the zero-based stage index, then reload the sky and ground colours, music, stage card and playfield font. A $FF pointer high byte marks the end of the stage table, so the index resets to the first terrain.
Background colours used above the horizon for each stage.
Background colours used below the horizon for each stage.

Copy the title font into the live character bank, lay out STAGE and two decimal digits, then read the stage name through the pointer table at $15B0. Copy name cells until $FF. Update the status panel and advance the intro animation before clearing projectile slots.
Nine display cells containing STAGE followed by four blank cells.
Twelve 16-bit pointers to the stage-card names, indexed by $4E8F.
High byte of the first little-endian name pointer. The printer uses this base to read the high byte for its selected stage.
Encoded text for the Moot banner. The stage-card printer stops at the $FF terminator.
Encoded text for the Geeza banner. The stage-card printer stops at the $FF terminator.
Encoded text for the Amar banner. The stage-card printer stops at the $FF terminator.

Encoded text for the Vicel banner. The stage-card printer stops at the $FF terminator.
Encoded text for the Nark banner. The stage-card printer stops at the $FF terminator.
Encoded text for the Absymbel banner. The stage-card printer stops at the $FF terminator.

Copy the forty-cell HUD template to $FBC0 and use white colour RAM. Write the two stage digits and refresh the score. When the timer is $99, draw one lives icon per remaining life. Otherwise write TIME followed by the timer's two BCD digits.
Forty screen codes for the stage and score row. The HUD renderer fills the timer or lives cells and writes the current digits over this template.
Leave the packed-decimal timer at its $99 sentinel once reached. Otherwise decrement the divider, reload it with 20 at zero and subtract one decimal unit from the timer.
Add A as packed decimal to the low score byte at $4EB5 and carry an increment into $4EB6 when it wraps.
Split the two packed-decimal score bytes into four digits, add $F1 to form screen codes and write the digits to $FBE2–$FBE5.
Replace the player sprites with the hit frames, move them up, hold and drop them, then wait before restarting their position. Subtract a life only if the training timer is at its $99 sentinel.

Require near depth and zero recovery countdown, then compare both axes of the player's cell position with bounds derived from the object's projected center and half-size. On hit queue sound effect $0B, animate the hit and arm the recovery countdown.

Find a free projectile slot and reject projected object coordinates outside the playable rectangle. Seed the shot at the object's center and calculate fractional velocities toward the player's projected position.
Scan four enemy projectile slots, use the animation phase to select a character rectangle and project its destination into screen memory through the row address tables.
Nine pointers to width-and-height character rectangles indexed by an enemy projectile's displayed phase.
High bytes of the projectile rectangle pointers, interleaved with the low bytes at $19D3.
Find an overlapping player shot, clear its straight-flight state, assign a randomized lateral velocity and negative vertical velocity, award one point unit and request effect 4.
On a hit from the projectile overlap test, change the object type to $0A and colour to 15, clear that projectile slot, add 3 to the packed-decimal score and queue effect 7.
Test four active shots for equal or one-adjacent depth and position within the bounds around the object's projected center. Return $FF and the shot slot in Y on a hit, or zero on a miss.
Sixteen match tolerances indexed by object depth. The shot test checks both screen axes within the indexed radius around the projected object.
Skip an inactive projectile slot and decrement the loop index. The path for an expired active slot starts at $1B60.
Scan four active player projectile slots, select a width-and-height character rectangle from its animation phase, and derive screen and colour destinations from the projected center.
Sixteen pointers to character rectangles used by the player projectile renderer at $1A9A.
Indexed high-byte operand for the player projectile shape table. The low-byte base is $1B6C.
5×3 screen-code rectangle for the player shot at phase indices 0, 1.
3×3 screen-code rectangle for the player shot at phase indices 2, 3.
3×3 screen-code rectangle for the player shot at phase indices 4, 5.
3×1 screen-code rectangle for the player shot at phase indices 6, 7.
1×1 screen-code rectangle for the player shot at phase indices 8, 9.
1×1 screen-code rectangle for the player shot at phase indices 10, 11.
1×1 screen-code rectangle for the player shot at phase indices 12, 13, 14, 15.

Decode the active-low direction bits in CIA1 port A. Produce bounded horizontal and vertical increments, with a stage-intro flag forcing descent. Edge-detect fire, then allocate one of four projectile slots and seed its coordinates from the player.
Convert the current sprite coordinates to the horizontal phase, horizon height and collision cells. Update the recovery flash and select both halves of the player shape for flight or running.
Fill the eight object-sort slots with their own indices.
Bidirectionally sort eight slot indices by the objects' depth bytes, repeating passes while a swap occurred.
Set CIA2 bits 0 and 1 to outputs and drive both low to choose VIC bank $C000. Select the $F800 screen, enable multicolour, and set sprite priorities and shared colours.
Index the stage's source character-set pointer then fall through to the bank copy.
Copy eight pages beginning at the source pointer $0D/$0E into $C000–$C7FF, the active playfield character bank.
Twelve stage pointers to six 2 KiB source character sets. The stage loader copies the selected set to bank $C000.
High-byte operand of the character-bank source pointer load. The low-byte operand is $1E35.
Set up the two player sprites at X $B8 with Y values separated by $15. Select shape pair $50/$51 and the player's two colours.
Shift the two-byte spawn seed and mix the high and low bytes through XOR and addition. Return the updated low byte in A.
Save the current low raster value and its doubled low byte. Read again while the doubled byte is zero.
Walk eight object slots and call a handler selected by the type byte of each slot.
Jump indirectly through $0D/$0E, retaining the caller's return address so the chosen handler returns to it.
Indexed jump table for updating each object's behaviour. Each type selects a handler while the slot index remains in X.
The indexed load at $1EAB reads the high byte of the handler pointer. Each low byte is immediately before it in the table at $1EBB.
Indexed table for selecting an object's frame directory from its type. The active object's depth indexes the selected directory.
The high-byte load at $342C indexes the same little-endian object frame table as the preceding low-byte load.
Apply horizontal steering, deflect overlapping shots, test near-depth player collision and decrement depth until the object is retired.
Select the motion triple at $1FC8, with an initial row of +7 lateral steps, and enter the shared motion reader.
Three pointers selected by handler $1FBA. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $1FBA. The first stored delta is $07.
Signed elevation deltas for object handler $1FBA. The first stored delta is $00.
Signed depth deltas for object handler $1FBA. The first stored delta is $FF.
Select the motion triple at $1FF8 and enter the shared motion reader, which adds deltas to position and depth.
Three pointers selected by handler $1FEA. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $1FEA. The first stored delta is $F9.
Signed elevation deltas for object handler $1FEA. The first stored delta is $00.
Signed depth deltas for object handler $1FEA. The first stored delta is $FF.
Copy the three motion table pointers beginning at $2028 to zero page and enter the shared path reader.
Three pointers selected by handler $201A. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $201A. The first stored delta is $05.
Signed elevation deltas for object handler $201A. The first stored delta is $00.
Signed depth deltas for object handler $201A. The first stored delta is $FF.
Read the path described by the pointer triple at $2067, which starts with zero lateral drift.
Three pointers selected by handler $2059. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $2059. The first stored delta is $05.
Signed elevation deltas for object handler $2059. The first stored delta is $00.
Signed depth deltas for object handler $2059. The first stored delta is $FF.
Select the pointer triple at $20A3. Its lateral and vertical delta streams begin at $20A9 and $20B9.
Three pointers selected by handler $2095. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $2095. The first stored delta is $00.
Signed elevation deltas for object handler $2095. The first stored delta is $00.
Signed depth deltas for object handler $2095. The first stored delta is $FF.

Apply the deltas indexed by movement count divided by four on each update, except at the restart marker. At count $14 or higher after increment, a hit lowers the colour byte. At colour 8, enter the explosion, clear the shot and advance the stage.
Signed lateral offsets for the single boss, with $80 at the end to restart at movement count $0C.
Signed elevation offsets stepped by the same count as the lateral stream at $213D.
Signed depth offsets for the single boss sequence at $20D7.
Walk a half-rate table of lateral and vertical deltas, rewind at its $80 marker and run the shot and player overlap checks.
Lateral offsets for the repeating path at $2179.
The first $80 here restarts the repeating path. Earlier values are signed elevation offsets.

Move the leading slot, check periodically for enemy fire and test incoming shots. Damage decrements the linked four colour bytes, then at colour 8 converts all four slots to explosion type and awards score units. The stage advances when its remaining count reaches zero.
Deflect incoming shots, look up elevation from the current depth, then add the depth direction. Reverse direction at depth zero or $0F.
Sixteen depth-indexed elevations for the object that bounces between depth zero and $0F.
Add the current depth's elevation delta before running the shared approach and collision path.
Elevation changes indexed by depth for the hopping object updater.
Read the current signed offsets from two tables and add them to the base coordinates of slot 7 to move the linked slot.
Add these signed lateral offsets to slot 7's position. The $80 marker ends the sequence.
Add these signed elevation offsets to the base elevation in slot 7.

Loop over the three boss head motion tables, fire periodically and test player shots. If a linked body is present, leave stage progression pending. Otherwise turn this slot into an explosion and advance the stage.
Signed lateral motion for the head handler. The $80 marker resets its path counter.
Signed elevation steps for the head's half-rate movement index.
Signed depth steps for the head's half-rate movement index.

Use half the slot's counter as an index into three signed displacement streams. Stop at a lateral $80 marker, otherwise add the lateral, vertical and depth deltas, test both collision directions and fire when the slot-offset counter reaches a multiple of 16.
Select the three streams at $23DA, $23EA and $23F9 and run the common object motion reader.
Three pointers selected by handler $23C6. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $23C6. The first stored delta is $EF.
Signed elevation deltas for object handler $23C6. The first stored delta is $F5.
Signed depth deltas for object handler $23C6. The first stored delta is $FF.
Select the movement tables through the pointer triple at $2416, including the lateral opening deltas $11 and $0A.
Three pointers selected by handler $2408. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $2408. The first stored delta is $11.
Signed elevation deltas for object handler $2408. The first stored delta is $F5.
Signed depth deltas for object handler $2408. The first stored delta is $FF.
Select the leftward path whose lateral stream begins at $245E and run the signed-displacement reader.
Three pointers selected by handler $244A. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $244A. The first stored delta is $EF.
Signed elevation deltas for object handler $244A. The first stored delta is $00.
Signed depth deltas for object handler $244A. The first stored delta is $FF.
Move with horizontal steering, reduce its elevation toward zero, test the player and projectile overlaps and retire the slot after its near-depth pass.
Test player projectiles and step toward depth 1. At that depth, rise by two per update while below the vertical cutoff.
Index the boss body offsets from $2510 using the movement count divided by four. Add its coordinate deltas and handle the $80 path marker.
Lateral motion deltas for the boss body update. The stream's $80 value takes its end-of-path branch.
Elevation deltas advanced by the boss body counter divided by four.
Depth adjustments for the boss body segment following the $2510 lateral stream.
Apply one of the half-rate delta records from $25EA, $2617 and $2643. The $80 first-stream value takes the shared restart path.
Apply the same half-rate path as the accompanying segments and fire periodically. A player shot reduces the boss count, changes its colour and advances the stage when the count reaches 8.
Half-rate lateral adjustments shared by the leading and following boss segments. The $80 marker resets the current path.
Signed elevation changes in the half-rate shared boss path.
Signed depth changes in the half-rate shared boss path.
Add the current horizontal steering increment, check projectile and player collisions, then step toward zero depth and retire the slot after depth underflows.

Advance the slot counter and use it to rewrite the frame selector at $35C6/$35C7. The active rectangle controls its projectile or deflection handling, and after the timed interval the object retreats and disappears.
Sixteen rectangle addresses selected by the timed hazard updater. The updater substitutes the selected pointer into the main depth directory.
The mutable frame selector reads one high byte from this base and the corresponding low byte from the base at $26D2.
Load the motion triple at $2700; that pattern starts with positive lateral increments of 6.
Three pointers selected by handler $26F2. The path reader treats them as lateral, elevation and depth delta streams, in that order.
Signed lateral deltas for object handler $26F2. The first stored delta is $06.

Find a free slot and select a spawn routine through the current stage and wave pointer arrays. When the primary spawn leaves the slot empty, a second stage table may supply an alternate spawn on even ticks.
One pointer per stage to a table of four alternate spawn handlers. The spawner's pseudo-random value masked with $06 selects the word.
The secondary spawner reads the high bytes at this base. Stage advance reads the same table to detect the end sentinel.
The $FFFF sentinel follows the twelve pointers. The stage advance routine sees the high $FF and wraps the zero-based stage index.

Every sixteenth spawn tick, dispatch through $2A02 using one low bit of the pseudo-random number.

Indexed high-byte base of the four path spawn pointers read by $2A06.
Initialize X's object with lateral offset zero, elevation 3, depth $0F, type $1C and colour 12. Clear the path counter.
Apply the common type $1C setup, then substitute type $1D to select a different motion path.
Apply the common path setup, then select type $1E and colour 11.
Apply the common path setup, then select type $1F with colour 11.
Apply the common path setup, then start at lateral offset $1A with type $20 and colour 14.
Freeze horizon drawing and wait for wave tick $64 and the first-spawn flag. Seed a type $1B boss at depth $0D, select the $8000 character bank and start the first boss tune.
Use wave-tick bits and the even-spawn check to choose a type $1A object at elevation 2 or 13, or a type $19 object at elevation 7.
Use the even-spawn tick gate, then seed type $37 at elevation 5 and colour 13.
Gate the spawn on tick and wave count, then choose a lateral offset and auxiliary movement byte using one random bit.
The two possible signed lateral offsets for the type $21 approach.
Two auxiliary path bytes associated with the lateral choices at $2B68.
Issue one of three type $18 positions from $2BA3 when the spawn tick's low three bits are zero.
Starting lateral offsets for the three members of the type $18 formation.
Spawn up to three type $17 objects in the wave, reading lateral offsets and auxiliary motion bytes from $2BDE and $2BE1.
Starting lateral offsets for the three members of the type $17 formation.
Auxiliary path bytes for the three consecutive type $17 spawns.
At the one-shot boss tick, load eight initial positions from tables, set two slots to type $16 and the others to $15, and select the $7800 character bank and first boss tune.
Initial signed lateral positions of the eight-slot formation.
Initial elevation cells for the eight-slot formation.
Initial depth bytes for the eight-slot formation.
Use the eight-slot boss initializer and substitute type $29 in slots 0 and 4.
On every fourth spawn tick up to a wave limit of 25, seed a distant type $14 object at elevation $14 and colour 15.
On even spawn ticks, seed a type $13 object at elevation zero and choose one of two saved colour values.
The two colours from which the type $13 even-tick spawner chooses.
Use the even-tick gate to seed a type $22 object at elevation 6 with colour 14.
Use the even-tick gate to seed a type $23 object at elevation 2 with colour 12.
At the one-shot boss tick, seed a type $2C leader and four type $2D objects, set their path phases to 0, 4, 8 and 12, and select the Moot character bank and the second boss tune.
Seed a type $25 leader with four type $26 objects and staggered path phases. Switch to the $9000 character bank and the second boss tune.
Seed a type $11 leader with four type $12 objects and staggered path phases. Switch to the $8800 character bank and the second boss tune.

Gate on the fourth spawn tick and cap the wave at five. Seed type $0E at lateral offset $69, elevation $0A and depth $0A.

Run the type $0C spawner and substitute type $35 and colour 15 if the slot is active.
Gate on the eighth spawn tick and limit the wave to eight. Seed type $0C at depth $0F and zero lateral and vertical offsets.
